lead.tldr: CFTC approval for Bitcoin perpetual futures creates regulated derivative market, unlocking institutional capital flow • Samsung's $408M stake in Dunamu validates South Korean exchange, may spur further corporate crypto exposure • CME's 24/7 Bitcoin futures eliminates weekend gaps, improving hedging efficiency for institutional traders • AI-driven DeFi attacks surge, raising security costs and deterring traditional finance from on‑chain migration • BlackRock iShares Bitcoin Trust sees $528M outflow, reflecting heightened risk aversion amid Middle East tensions • UniCredit warns MiCA lacks robust deposit insurance, leaving stablecoin reserves vulnerable in a crypto‑bank shock

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The CFTC’s green light for regulated bitcoin perpetual futures marks a U.S. derivatives framework while Samsung’s $408 million stake in Upbit underscores corporate confidence. Meanwhile, Bitcoin slipped below $73,000 amid Middle‑East tensions, triggering near‑$1 billion in liquidations and prompting scrutiny of market stability.

top_signals.title: U.S. CFTC opens crypto 'perp' door with first approval at regulated firm
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission has issued its first approval for bitcoin perpetual futures on a regulated exchange. The approval authorizes the exchange Kalshi to list the contract identified as BTCPERP. It also permits a Coinbase affiliate to direct U.S. customers to global options and perpetual contracts. The ruling creates a regulatory framework for crypto derivatives in the United States and is viewed as a significant step toward broader market adoption.

top_signals.title: Samsung units to acquire $408 million stake in Upbit operator Dunamu
top_signals.summary: Samsung’s various units are acquiring a $408 million equity stake in Dunamu, the operator of the Upbit cryptocurrency exchange. The investment represents a significant corporate endorsement of South Korea’s cryptocurrency market. The capital infusion is expected to strengthen Dunamu’s balance sheet and support its growth initiatives.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin drops below $73,000 as U.S. strikes on Iran spark $1 billion liquidations
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin slipped below the $73,000 threshold following U.S. airstrikes on Iran, triggering a broad sell‑off across the cryptocurrency market. The price decline generated nearly $1 billion in leveraged liquidations, highlighting the sensitivity of margin‑based strategies to sudden risk events. Long positions were the primary source of the wipe‑out, with Bitcoin and Ether together accounting for the majority of the losses. The episode underscores the importance for institutional investors of monitoring geopolitical developments and managing exposure to leveraged crypto assets.

top_signals.title: Samsung is buying a $408 million stake in South Korea’s biggest crypto exchange
top_signals.summary: Samsung affiliates are purchasing a 4% equity stake in Dunamu, the operator of South Korea’s largest cryptocurrency exchange Upbit, for $408 million. The transaction lowers Kakao’s ownership after Kakao disposed of roughly $1.5 billion of equity in the exchange within a month. The move signals Samsung’s continued strategic interest in the crypto sector and may influence the competitive dynamics of the region’s leading digital‑asset platform.

top_signals.title: CME ends bitcoin weekend gaps with launch of 24/7 futures trading from Friday
top_signals.summary: CME Group has started 24/7 trading of Bitcoin futures and options on its Globex platform. This eliminates the traditional weekend market closure that produced the “CME gap.” The continuous trading window gives institutional investors the ability to hedge positions at any time while the exchange still observes a short maintenance period on Saturday.

top_signals.title: Wall Street’s trillion-dollar dilemma: Why AI-powered hackers are keeping big banks off the blockchain
top_signals.summary: CertiK’s chief executive has warned that AI driven attacks made April the worst month for decentralized finance security in four years. The attacks were recorded on 27 of the 30 days in that month. High profile incidents include a $1.46 billion breach of Bybit and roughly $600 million stolen from Drift Protocol and Kelp Dao. These losses are prompting large banks and other Wall Street firms to pause or limit the migration of trillions of dollars onto blockchain platforms.

top_signals.title: IBIT news: BlackRock bitcoin ETF sheds $528 million, the second-largest daily outflow on record
top_signals.summary: BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust experienced a net outflow of $528 million, marking the second‑largest single‑day withdrawal since the fund’s inception. The broader U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF market also saw outflows totaling $733 million on the same day. The withdrawals occurred as Bitcoin fell below $73,000 amid heightened Middle‑East tensions, prompting forced sales of the fund’s underlying Bitcoin and raising liquidity concerns for institutional investors.

top_signals.title: UniCredit warns Europe may struggle to contain crypto-bank crisis under MiCA rules
top_signals.summary: UniCredit, a leading European bank, has warned that the EU’s deposit‑insurance framework may not be robust enough to absorb a crypto‑bank shock under the new MiCA rules. The bank points to a gap between the EU’s partial guarantees and the broader protection offered in the United States. Without full‑coverage deposit guarantees, large stablecoin reserve accounts could be exposed to significant losses if a crisis hits the crypto‑banking sector. Institutional investors therefore need to reassess the resilience of their stablecoin holdings and related liquidity strategies in Europe.

top_signals.title: VanEck’s tokenized VBILL US Treasury fund can now be used as collateral on Euler
top_signals.summary: VanEck’s tokenized VBILL US Treasury fund has been added to Euler’s list of accepted collateral assets. This integration enables token holders to borrow against the Treasury‑backed token on Euler’s decentralized finance lending platform. The development bridges traditional fixed‑income securities with DeFi, offering institutional investors a new way to leverage low‑risk government debt in crypto‑based liquidity strategies.

top_signals.title: Grayscale IPO delayed as crypto firms reassess public market plans
top_signals.summary: Grayscale, one of the largest crypto asset managers, has postponed its planned U.S. IPO until at least Q4 2026 because of weak market conditions and low investor demand. The postponement signals a broader cooling of the crypto IPO market. Other crypto firms such as Payward, ConsenSys and Ledger are also delaying their public listings, underscoring the sector’s current challenges for institutional investors.

top_signals.title: Sui blockchain suffers another network outage as transactions grind to a halt
top_signals.summary: The Sui mainnet suffered its second outage of the year, bringing transaction processing to a complete halt. The disruption triggered an 8% decline in the SUI token price within 24 hours. Mysten Labs’ core team is actively investigating the root cause of the failure. The incident underscores reliability risks for developers and institutional investors who depend on Sui’s high‑performance infrastructure for decentralized applications.

First, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission gave its inaugural approval for bitcoin perpetual futures on a regulated exchange. Kalshi will now list the BTCPERP contract and a Coinbase affiliate can point U.S. customers to global options and perpetual products. This regulatory foothold creates a clearer path for derivatives and could accelerate institutional participation. Second, Samsung’s various business units announced a $408 million equity purchase in Dunamu, the company behind the Upbit exchange. The deal marks a major corporate vote of confidence in South Korea’s crypto ecosystem and provides Dunamu with a strong balance sheet to fund product expansion and cross‑border initiatives. Third, Bitcoin slipped below $73,000 after U.S. airstrikes on Iran, triggering almost $1 billion in leveraged liquidations. The sharp sell‑off reminded us how quickly geopolitical events can ripple through margin‑based strategies and why robust risk controls remain essential for any institutional portfolio.
